Right: the same graph without the C-D edge (drawn dashed in the accent color), which leaves two separate pieces even with directions ignored, so is_weakly_connected() returns False." width="100%"} A directed graph is weakly connected if the underlying undirected graph (ignoring edge directions) is connected. Equivalently, there is a path between every pair of nodes when edge directions are ignored. For undirected graphs, this is equivalent to checking regular connectivity (same as `is_connected()`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is weakly connected, `False` otherwise. Empty graphs are considered weakly connected (vacuously true). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Weak connectivity ignores edge orientation: the check is whether the *underlying* undirected graph is connected, which BFS or DFS decides in $O(V + E)$. Weakly connected is therefore strictly weaker than strongly connected, so any strongly-connected graph is also weakly connected but not conversely. Empty graphs pass vacuously. For undirected inputs the notion collapses to `is_connected()`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Even though both edges point toward `B` (so `A` can't reach `C` directly), the graph is still weakly connected because ignoring direction links everything together: ::: {#9fe4dd77 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("C", "B"), # All connected when ignoring direction ] ) ) # Returns True graph.is_weakly_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#e8fc6138 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False (can't reach C from A while respecting edge direction) graph.is_strongly_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Two completely separate components fail weak connectivity too, since ignoring direction doesn't create edges that don't exist: ::: {#a1ef040f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "X", "Y"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("X", "Y")]) ) # Returns False graph.is_weakly_connected() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: :::
